data_output.description: encode(splits) returns (encoded, dimension). For every split, encoded[split] remains (features, labels, users). features is a globally offset np.int32 matrix in canonical selected source-row order with exact columns [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, user_id_tab]. The sixth raw categorical value is exactly the Python tuple (row[1], row[3]), where row[1] is raw user_id and row[3] is raw tab from the log. All six vocabularies are fit only on splits["train"], each has one unknown bucket, and validation/test unseen user_id_tab tuples use the sixth unknown bucket. labels remain None for test when include_test_labels=False; users remains the raw user_id vector.

model_input.description: Model receives globally offset integer feature matrices of shape (N, 6). logits is bias + sum of the six corresponding scalar weights. step() receives equal-shape positive and negative matrices with exactly six columns and optimizes the unchanged pairwise logistic loss.

feature_engineer.objective: Append exactly one train-fitted categorical user_id-by-tab interaction feature to the encoded additive feature matrix while retaining the existing five encoded fields in their current order.
required_changes: Keep load() row tuples and raw CSV reads unchanged: use only raw fields user_id and tab from each log row for the new interaction; do not read any additional source column or file.

In encode(), retain the existing first five raw values in exactly this order: row[1] (user_id), row[2] (video_id), row[3] (tab), row[4] (hour), row[5] (weekday). Append the sixth raw categorical value as the tuple (row[1], row[3]), representing exactly (user_id, tab).

Fit the sixth vocabulary exclusively by iterating training rows, exactly as the existing categorical vocabularies are fitted. Its vocabulary keys must be tuple values (user_id, tab); do not stringify, hash, or derive an alternate alias for either source field.

Give the sixth field one unknown bucket at index len(vocab), use that bucket for every validation or test (user_id, tab) tuple absent from the training-fitted sixth vocabulary, and retain the existing per-field offset recipe: offsets = cumulative sum of preceding field dimensions.

Return features as int32 with shape (number_of_split_rows, 6), preserving the selected source-row order for train, valid, and test. Keep users as row[1] in that same order and preserve existing label handling, including test labels being None when include_test_labels=False.
Return the total embedding dimension as the sum of all six field dimensions.
preserve: Keep SPLITS, date filtering, label policy, hour derivation from hourmin, weekday derivation from date, and max_rows_per_split behavior unchanged.
Use no forbidden, excluded, quarantined, outcome, aggregate, or test-label-derived input. The only new feature must use eligible raw user_id and tab.
Do not change train.py, model.py, or config.json.
Do not reorder or alter the semantics of the five pre-existing feature columns.
coordination_notes: The shared encoded interface becomes encoded[split] = (features, labels, users), where features is int32 shape (N, 6), with columns [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, user_id_tab], each already globally offset and in range [0, dimension).
The model_designer will update model.py to accept this six-column additive input. No trainer change is required because train.py forwards feature matrices unchanged.
The interaction is categorical and train-fitted only; validation and test unseen pairs must map to the one sixth-field unknown bucket rather than expanding the vocabulary.

model_designer.objective: Adapt the additive pairwise ranker to consume the six-field matrix produced by data.py, adding no nonlinear or non-additive model architecture beyond summing the new user_id_tab categorical weight.
required_changes: In Model.step(), replace the fixed five-column validation with a six-column validation: raise ValueError unless positive_features.shape[1] == 6. Keep the existing requirements that both pair matrices are two-dimensional, have identical shapes, and have nonzero pair count.
Keep logits(features) as bias plus self.weights[features].sum(1), so the score is exactly the additive sum of six categorical field weights plus the unchanged bias.

Keep the existing pairwise logistic objective, gradient construction with np.add.at for positive and negative feature IDs, L2 regularization, Adam constants and update logic, finite-value checks, prediction batching, and state/load_state behavior unchanged.
Do not add interaction layers, embeddings, cross terms, alternative losses, altered optimizer settings, or configuration defaults.
preserve: Preserve pairwise logistic training semantics and the additive scorer; the sole added capacity is the sixth categorical user_id_tab feature weight supplied by data.py.
Preserve learning_rate and l2 constructor defaults exactly; config.json is unchanged and must not be compensated for through model defaults.
Preserve prediction output shape: predict(features) must return one finite one-dimensional score per input row in input order.
Do not change data.py, train.py, or config.json.
coordination_notes: Expect feature matrices from data.py with exact columns [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, user_id_tab] and total dimension covering six offset categorical vocabularies.

train.py already uses the encoded matrices for same-user K=4 uniform negative sampling, validation-only proxy/checkpoint selection, and canonical prediction emission; it requires no edit for the six-column interface.
The updated six-column check is necessary for the contract probe and full training to reject stale five-column encodings.

reasoning: The requested ablation is exactly one train-fitted categorical interaction between the eligible raw log fields user_id and tab. It requires data.py to create and encode that sixth field and model.py to accept six additive IDs. train.py and config.json already preserve K=4 same-user uniform negative sampling, pairwise logistic loss, optimizer, regularization, validation-only early stopping/checkpoint selection, and canonical valid/test prediction archive generation, so activating trainer would be unnecessary and risks changing the controlled ablation.
